clue.text: Teacher I stood up, bit of a looker?

indicators.note: in a down entry, something stood up is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher confesses to having been stood up by someone rather attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looker' suggests a pretty person, but here it is the eye, and the coloured ring of the eye is a part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is the coloured part of the eye, so it is literally a piece of the organ that does the looking.

clue.text: Indication in slang isn't taken the wrong way

indicators.note: read the wrong way means read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a hint in slang is not being misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal is a sign or gesture that conveys information, which is what an indication does.

clue.text: Demon not proving fiendish in North American city

indicators.note: fiendish suggests something devilishly twisted, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demon that fails to be wicked turns up in a city across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital of the Canadian province of Alberta, a city on the North American continent.

clue.text: Bloomer feeding you to ferocious animals

indicators.note: food goes inside an animal, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: crocs is the short form of crocodiles
U sounds like you, as in text speak

explanation.surface: A blunder that ends with you being thrown to wild beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a mistake, and the surface uses that sense; the definition means something that blooms. U for you is a standard crossword substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a spring flower, so it is something that blooms: a bloomer in the crossword sense.

clue.text: I'm a twerp to rectify distortion of science-fiction

indicators.note: to rectify is to put right, so these letters are rearranged into a proper order

parts.note: every letter of the phrase is used

explanation.surface: Someone admits being an idiot and offers to fix a glitch in a sci-fi story.
explanation.definitionFit: In science fiction, a disruption of the normal flow of hours and years that moves characters between eras is a staple plot device.

clue.text: Crayon made from petals?

indicators.note: something made from materials is built out of them in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: all six letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether a soft colouring stick could be produced out of flower parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the whimsy: pastel colours are pale and petal-like.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a stick of chalky colouring material used for drawing, much like a crayon.

clue.text: Giant rolling up a stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, rolling up means travelling from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A giant pushes a boulder up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is an informal adjective for something huge or enormous in size or scale.

clue.text: Note written about a surplus

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a reminder is a written note to prompt the memory
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone jots down a memo concerning an excess.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder is what is left over after the rest has been used, which is an excess or leftover amount.

clue.text: Sailor in river, airmen flying over

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other
aircraft flying over are tossed about in the air, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the six letters are rearranged around the single letter
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A seaman on a river watches as pilots pass overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who works on ships at sea, so a synonym for sailor.

clue.text: Freebooter losing head, furious

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a freebooter is a plunderer at sea

explanation.surface: A buccaneer about to be beheaded is understandably enraged.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means very angry, so it is a direct synonym for being in a fury.

clue.text: Things wrong with cast: error in group of players

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are in the wrong places and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written into the mix
taken as written into the mix
taken as written into the mix

explanation.surface: A theatre company confesses that its actors botched things.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads cast and players as actors in a play; the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A string orchestra is an ensemble of violinists, violists, cellists and bassists, so a band of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Underwear in record time!

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone strips to their vest in a sprint that sets a new best.
explanation.walkthrough: A singlet is the British term for a sleeveless vest worn under a shirt or for running.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, a garment often worn beneath a shirt as an undergarment.

clue.text: Crook in workforce?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shepherd's hooked stick
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: A question whether there is a criminal among the employees.
explanation.walkthrough: Crook reads as a villain, but here it is the shepherd's hooked stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a long walking stick or crook and the body of people employed by a company.

clue.text: Superficial swine passing round room

indicators.note: passing round means going all the way around something, enclosing it

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A shallow pig wanders around a chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow describes something lacking depth of thought or feeling, which is what superficial means.

clue.text: Eye ticker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to look at closely, as a verb
second meaning: a timepiece that ticks

explanation.walkthrough: Ticker is slang for the heart, which pairs with eye as body parts; here it is a clock worn on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for observing attentively and a noun for a small timepiece worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Giant ear can flap in the winds

indicators.note: winds is read as the verb, twisting things round into a new order

parts.note: every letter of the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge ear flapping in a breeze, which is just what a big beast's ear does.
explanation.walkthrough: Winds looks like a noun for breezes, but it is a verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: The African elephant is the largest living land animal, so it is a natural example of a giant.

clue.text: Hasty touch coming round ends in unfortunate goal

indicators.note: coming round means circling something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a caress is a gentle touch

indicators.note: ends in asks for the final letter of each of the next words

parts.note: the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A rushed contact on the ball leads to an unlucky own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless action is done without due thought or attention, much as a hasty one is rushed.

clue.text: Binder with uglier tab cut off

indicators.note: off means not right or awry, so the letters are rearranged
cut means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written into the mix
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A folder whose ugly label has been snipped away.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligature is a cord or thread used for tying something tightly, so it is a thing that binds.

clue.text: Bitter about a rocker's rival being fashionable

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer, an ale
taken as written
in 1960s Britain mods and rockers were rival youth gangs

explanation.surface: A resentful biker is jealous of a trendy rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter looks like an adjective for resentful, but it is the British beer. Mods were sharp-dressed scooter riders who clashed with leather-clad rockers.
explanation.definitionFit: A la mode is a French phrase borrowed into English meaning in the current style or trend.

clue.text: On being consumed by deluge, flattened

indicators.note: something consumed is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a deluge is a great flood
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Swept up in a torrent, someone is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: To be floored is to be knocked to the ground, so flat out, or figuratively stunned and beaten.

clue.text: Strange issue likely

parts.note: odd means strange
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: A peculiar problem is probably going to arise.
explanation.walkthrough: Odds-on is a betting term for an outcome more likely than not.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on favourite is expected to win, so the term describes something probable.

clue.text: Hanging head in disgrace, unknown have-nots turned up

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the have-nots are the poor
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A shamed man hangs his head as some anonymous paupers arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanging head looks like one phrase, but hanging alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Droopy describes something sagging or dangling limply downwards, which is what hanging means here.

clue.text: Giant back in pig, returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so read from right to left
in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a hog is a pig
the tail is at the back

explanation.surface: A huge creature is put back into the pigsty.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath is the Philistine giant slain by David in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath, the biblical giant, has become a common noun for any person or thing of enormous size.

clue.text: German songs governor listened to?

indicators.note: listened to means the word is heard, so we go by its sound

parts.note: a governor is a leader, and the German word is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A question whether a ruler paid attention to some German music.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder is the German plural for songs, used in English for Romantic art songs by Schubert and others.

clue.text: Unremarkable location of white lines?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, cryptic: where the painted centre markings run along a street

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: the painted lines dividing traffic lanes run down the centre of the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes views or tastes that avoid extremes and so are bland, and literally the centre of a street.

clue.text: Wise guys, most are genuinely ignorant, first of all

indicators.note: first of all asks for the opening letter of every word in the phrase

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A cynic remarks that most so-called experts are really clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magi are the three wise men of the Nativity story.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the wise men from the East who visited the infant Jesus, so learned men.

clue.text: Act the same either way

parts.note: surface reading: behave consistently whatever happens
setter's reading: a word for an act that reads identically forwards and backwards

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is advice on consistent behaviour; read literally, it asks for a synonym of act whose letters run the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an action or feat, and its four letters form a palindrome.

clue.text: Obscene amount before tax deducted

definitions.meaning: second meaning: total earnings before any deductions

explanation.surface: A complaint that a pre-tax salary is indecently large.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means crude or disgusting and also describes a total income figure before stoppages are taken off.

clue.text: Soldier on manoeuvres ever trailing as such

indicators.note: trailing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: per se is Latin for as such or in itself

indicators.note: manoeuvres moves things about, so the letters are repositioned

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier on exercises keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: Soldier on looks like a soldier at manoeuvres, but it is a verb phrase meaning keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere is to continue steadily despite difficulty, which is what soldiering on means as an idiom.
